content: CSS cascade precedence for extension styles overriding a host app (MDN @layer): normal unlayered declarations BEAT all normal layered declarations, so putting extension CSS in an @layer makes it lose to the host page. For !important the layer order reverses and layered !important beats unlayered !important. Practical consequence for a content script: @layer is the wrong tool for overriding host styles; either match/exceed host specificity or use a narrow, deliberate !important. Content script CSS is author-origin and competes normally with page CSS.
